title: Variables, Handlers, Conditions, and Control
objective: Control playbook behavior with variables, facts, conditions, tags, blocks, delegation, and secrets.

paragraphs: Variables can come from plays, inventory, host_vars, group_vars, facts, registered results, prompts, and extra vars. Precedence resolves conflicts, but simple ownership is easier to reason about than relying on overrides.

Jinja expressions and when clauses make tasks conditional. register captures results; changed_when and failed_when refine semantics. Blocks group work and can provide rescue and always paths, while tags select subsets.

Vault encrypts secrets at rest, not during use. Delegation and local actions move a task to another host; wait_for coordinates availability. Environment values should be scoped as narrowly as practical.
explanation.rule: Make conditions explicit, keep secret values encrypted, and avoid clever precedence chains.

examples.title: Conditional Notification
examples.code:
- name: Configure service
  hosts: app
  tasks:
    - name: Render config
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: app.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/app.conf
      when: app_enabled
      notify: Restart app
examples.note: A boolean variable gates the task; a change notifies the handler.
